## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format and validation manifest

## Description

Defines the packaging format that curated tutorials use so they are versioned and
testable independently of Dashboard releases. The format covers the three elements
the strategy names: tutorial metadata, pinned images, and a validation manifest.
It is the shared artifact that both the Dashboard tutorial gallery (which lists
tutorials from their metadata and launches them using their pinned images) and the
authored tutorial content (which is packaged and validated per the format) build
against.

## Scope

- Define the metadata that describes a packaged tutorial, sufficient for a gallery
  to list it and a consumer to understand what it covers.
- Define how tutorial images are pinned so that launching a tutorial is
  reproducible against a known target release.
- Define the validation manifest used to test a packaged tutorial, so each
  tutorial can be validated against the current release on its own cadence,
  independently of Dashboard release cycles.
- Define versioning rules for packaged tutorials.
- Publish the format specification where the Dashboard gallery implementers and
  the tutorial authoring teams can build against it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format is documented and covers metadata, pinned images, and a
  validation manifest, as required by the strategy.
- A tutorial packaged in the format can be versioned and validated independently
  of a Dashboard release: running its validation manifest against a target
  release produces a deterministic pass/fail result.
- The format specification is reviewed and agreed by the teams that build against
  it — the Dashboard gallery implementers and the tutorial authoring teams —
  before dependent work consumes it.
- The format specification is committed to an accessible platform repository.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1 — tutorial packaging format). This epic is prioritized P0 by
  inheritance: the gallery and all curated tutorials build against the format,
  so it gates the strategy's P0 delivery.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch

## Description

Adds the curated tutorial gallery to the Dashboard: a section of the console that
lists maintained, tested tutorials and lets a user launch one into their own
project with a single click — opening a workbench pre-loaded with the tutorial
notebook, or importing the tutorial pipeline into the project.

## Scope

- Gallery surface in the Dashboard that lists curated tutorials from their
  packaging metadata.
- One-click launch mechanics for notebook tutorials: create a workbench in the
  user's project with the tutorial notebook available in it.
- One-click launch mechanics for pipeline tutorials: import the tutorial pipeline
  into the user's project.
- Validation of the passive components this launch path exercises: the workbench
  path (Notebook CR creation and reconciliation) and the pipeline import path
  (KFP v2 API) must keep working with no code changes in those components —
  their behavior is verified through this epic's launch acceptance criteria.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can open the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard and see the curated
  tutorials listed with their metadata.
- Launching a notebook tutorial from the gallery creates a workbench in the
  user's project containing the tutorial notebook, and the workbench reaches a
  healthy running state (this validates the workbench path end to end).
- Launching a pipeline tutorial from the gallery imports the pipeline into the
  user's project, and the imported pipeline is visible and runnable (this
  validates the pipeline import path end to end).
- End-to-end launch is verified with at least one tutorial packaged in the
  defined tutorial packaging format.
- The gallery can be disabled through the Dashboard's existing configuration
  surface without affecting other Dashboard functionality, providing a rollback
  path for the new surface.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0 — tutorial gallery with one-click launch into the user's project).

# Curated notebook tutorials for core getting-started journeys

## Description

Authors the notebook-based curated tutorials covering the core getting-started
journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, and
first RAG app. Each tutorial is packaged in the tutorial packaging format
(metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) and tested against the current
release, so the set stays maintained as the platform evolves.

## Scope

- Author five notebook-based tutorials covering: first workbench, data prep,
  first training run, first deployment, first RAG app.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format so it is versioned and
  independently testable.
- Test each tutorial against the current release via its validation manifest and
  keep the set maintained.
- Verify the workbench journey behaves as the tutorials describe — the tutorial
  content doubles as validation that the workbench (passive component) keeps
  working as documented for a new user following the journey.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist covering the listed journeys, each packaged per
  the tutorial packaging format.
- Each tutorial passes its validation manifest against the current release.
- Each tutorial runs end to end in a clean project: a user following it reaches
  the journey's outcome (workbench created, data prepared, training run
  completed, model deployed, RAG application running).
- Tutorials are versioned independently of Dashboard releases.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0 — six curated, tested tutorials): covers the five notebook-based
  journeys; the pipeline-based journey is covered by the pipeline tutorial epic.

# Gallery usage and tutorial contribution documentation

## Description

Documents the tutorial gallery for users and contributors: how to find and
launch tutorials from the gallery, and how to contribute new tutorials. Written
after the gallery and tutorial set are implemented, so the documentation
describes what was actually built.

## Scope

Content outline:

- **Using the tutorial gallery** — a user-facing topic covering what the gallery
  is, how to open it, and how to launch a notebook tutorial (workbench with the
  notebook) or a pipeline tutorial (imported pipeline) into a project.
- **Contributing new tutorials** — a contributor-facing topic covering the
  contribution process: how a tutorial is packaged (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest per the tutorial packaging format), how it is validated
  against a release, and what is expected of a maintained tutorial.
  Documentation only — tutorial submission tooling and community/partner intake
  are out of scope for this release, as is localization of tutorial content.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers both using the gallery and the contribution process for
  new tutorials, per the strategy's documentation requirement.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery and
  the shipped tutorial set; steps and described behavior match what was built.
- The documentation is published in the platform documentation.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2 — documentation for gallery usage and tutorial contribution).
  Epic priority is P1 per the docs-authoring priority exception, derived from
  the strategy's overall priority (Major).

# RHAISTRAT-9019 Decomposition — Curated getting-started tutorial gallery

Strategy: RHAISTRAT-9019 (Curated getting-started tutorial gallery, priority Major,
status Refinement Done).

Triage: full decomposition. The strategy is not below threshold — its problem
statement explicitly identifies three architecturally distinct work streams with
different owners and review processes (product code for the gallery and launch
mechanics, substantive content authoring of the tutorials themselves, and
documentation), spanning multiple components and teams. It is not documentation-only.

All components referenced by the strategy (Dashboard, Notebooks, Data Science
Pipelines) have architecture-context files in `.context/architecture-context/`
(rhoai-3.0), so no onboarding chains or provisioning investigations are required.
Notebooks and Data Science Pipelines are **passive** components in this strategy:
the launch mechanics use their existing, documented interfaces (Notebook CRD via
the Dashboard; KFP v2 pipeline import), so no code changes are needed in them.
Their validation is folded in as acceptance criteria on the gallery launch epic
and the tutorial testing epics; because the validating teams (Workbenches, RHOAI
Pipelines) own the tutorial content epics that exercise those paths, no separate
validation epics are generated.

## Epic List

|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E001 | Tutorial packaging format and validation manifest | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E002 | Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E003 | Curated notebook tutorials for core getting-started journeys | Implementation | Workbenches | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E004 | First-pipeline tutorial | Implementation | RHOAI Pipelines | P0 |

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections (non-blocking):** the strategy has no Impacted Teams
  table, no Dependencies table, no formal Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and
  no non-functional requirements section. Teams were inferred from the
  architecture-context owning teams (Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard, Notebooks →
  Workbenches, Data Science Pipelines → RHOAI Pipelines; the Documentation team
  has no context file and was assigned by convention). Acceptance criteria below
  were derived from the HLRs.
- **Priority inheritance, not inversion:** HLR-3 is labeled P1, but its epic (E001)
  is P0 because every P0 deliverable (gallery and tutorials) builds against the
  format. This is standard prerequisite priority inheritance, flagged here for
  reviewer visibility.
- **Scope trap — RAG journey (architecture claim uncorroborated):** HLR-2 includes
  a "first RAG app" tutorial, but no architecture-context file covers a RAG
  capability in the platform (no context file exists for Llama Stack or any other
  RAG-bearing component). The tutorial epic is unaffected — it is authored either
  way — but if no supported RAG surface exists at release time, that one tutorial
  may need to build the RAG app from generic workbench/serving primitives or be
  descoped. Verify during epic refinement; this does not change the epic DAG.
- **Component mapping note (E001):** the packaging format is consumed by the
  Dashboard gallery implementation and by both tutorial-content epics, so its work
  spans several strategy components. It is assigned the single canonical component
  `Dashboard` as the most-relevant consumer (the gallery parses the metadata and
  launch mechanics use the pinned images), owned by RHOAI Dashboard.
- **Epic-size watch item (E003):** E003 bundles five curated, tested tutorials
  (authoring + packaging + release testing) and sits at the upper bound of the
  ~2-week guideline. It is kept as one epic because it is a single logical
